scope: 30 cold independent HTML-reading judgements, same question and HTML; 10 personas x3 attempts; account/runtime available; no observed user success or time
question_change: Numeric example score removed from JSON format instruction to avoid response anchoring; HTML, persona descriptions, star definitions and substantive question unchanged.
question:
Claude Desktop is already installed and your account has Cowork access. No course folder or previous course conversation exists. There is no trainer. You are trying this on your own.

Below is actual HTML from the published handbook: navigation, cover, Start and Prework. Cowork is selected; other runtime content is hidden and omitted. Pause/Resume panels are initially closed, so only their labels are shown here. The rest of the handbook, including linked reading destinations, exists beyond this excerpt. Assess the start, not omitted later material. This is an HTML-reading simulation, not actual app execution or a visual screenshot test.

Imagine your first start. What would you actually do, in order? Would you get going? Would it feel 'really snappy and obvious'? Where would you hesitate, detour, ask for help or stop? Do not invent app behaviour or claim you actually executed anything. Do not be polite for the author.

Give 1–5 stars for how quick and obvious the start feels: 1=cannot get going; 2=need substantial help; 3=can get going with detours; 4=clear with minor hesitation; 5=snappy and obvious throughout. Rate the route to the first visible result (the game), not full prework completion or course quality. Report getting going separately from smoothness. Quote the exact instruction behind your most important hesitation, and name the ONE change that would improve the start most.

Under 250 words. Return a JSON object with these fields: stars (integer from 1 to 5), wouldGetGoing (yes, no, or uncertain), firstActions (array), hesitations (array), evidenceQuote (exact instruction text), feeling (in your own voice), biggestImprovement (text).
